 ## Methodology Principles
 
-- **Separate latency from capacity:** Low-concurrency runs (`C = 1–4`) measure end-to-end RTT and expose client-server stack affinity; capacity conclusions require checking both server CPU saturation and client headroom.
-- **Zero-error gating:** Every client validates response lengths, streaming message counts, aggregate bytes, and terminal `OK` status; any error invalidates the run.
-- **Honest multi-process aggregation:** Multi-process runs report aggregate throughput and server CPU while keeping merged latency percentiles `null` rather than incorrectly averaging independent histograms.
-- **Transparent variance:** All tables report round medians and all Benchkit charts show the full observed min–max range across rounds.
+- **Synchronized warmup & unbiased throughput:** All three load generators (`go/client`, `rust-tonic`, `native-cpp/load.h`) connect eagerly, synchronize workers on a post-warmup monotonic barrier, and compute unbiased per-worker active-time throughput `sum(completed_i / active_seconds_i)`.
+- **Zero-allocation O(1) latency histograms:** Clients record latencies in a fixed-memory log-linear histogram (8-bit mantissa, <0.4% error, exact below 512 ns) rather than growing and sorting multi-million-element arrays after measurement.
+- **Fair thread budgets & payload handling:** All servers align concurrency/polling budgets with `SERVER_THREADS` / CPU affinity and avoid artificial per-RPC channel ping-pong or avoidable heap churn.
+- **Zero-error gating & transparent variance:** Every client validates response lengths, streaming message counts, aggregate bytes, and terminal `OK` status; any error fails the run. Reports present round medians with observed min–max bounds.

 # RPC Framework Performance Report
 
-> **Campaign:** `2026-11-21-full-af19148`  |  **Formal Runs:** 906 (+ 302 smoke)  |  **Completed RPCs:** 563,735,713  |  **Errors:** 0
->
-> **Host:** AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX (16 physical cores / 32 threads, `performance` governor, Linux x86_64, localhost TCP)  
-> **Charts:** Generated via [Benchkit](https://github.com/open-s4c/benchkit) (`benchkit.lwchart`) in both PNG and vector PDF — see [`harness/plot_report.py`](../harness/plot_report.py) to regenerate.
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> **Status: Awaiting Fresh Post-Fix Benchmark Run**  
+> All pre-`2026-11-25` benchmark datasets and reports have been **archived and marked invalidated（作废）** after a full code audit uncovered implementation defects that materially skewed measurements across frameworks.
 
 ---
 
-## Executive Summary
+## Why Pre-Fix Data Was Invalidated
 
-This report evaluates **8 RPC server stacks** across three independent, zero-error benchmark matrices on the same machine:
+The following defects existed in all benchmark runs prior to `2026-11-25` and have now been fixed in `workloads/` and `harness/`:
 
-1. **Native Cross-Protocol Matrix (360 runs, 191.8M RPCs):** Plaintext closed-loop C++ clients comparing **Apache Thrift**, **Cap'n Proto**, **brpc (`baidu_std`)**, **grpc-lite (`af19148`)**, **Tonic**, **gRPC C++ (callback)**, **gRPC C++ (sync)**, and **gRPC-Go** across latency, concurrency, multicore scaling, large payloads, and asymmetric payloads.
-2. **Extended gRPC Matrix (420 runs, 276.2M RPCs):** Five gRPC server configurations tested with both **gRPC-Go** and **Tonic** multi-process load generators across **Plaintext vs. certificate-verified TLS**, **1 / 4 / 8 server cores**, **1 KiB vs. 64 KiB**, and **all 4 RPC modes** (unary, client-stream, server-stream, bidi ping-pong).
-3. **`grpc-lite` TLS Backend Evolution (126 runs, 95.8M RPCs):** Controlled same-host comparison of historical `a20631f` (mbedTLS) → `af19148` (mbedTLS 3.6.6) → `af19148` (OpenSSL 4.0.3).
-
-### Headline Findings
-
-| Dimension | Winner in This Setup | Headline Metric (Median of 3 × 5 s Rounds) | Key Takeaway |
-| --- | --- | --- | --- |
-| **Lowest 1 KiB Latency (C=1, 1 core)** | **Apache Thrift** | **15.5 µs** P50 / **20.1 µs** P99 | Non-HTTP/2 binary protocols (`Thrift`, `Cap'n Proto`, `brpc`) run at roughly half the latency of gRPC stacks. |
-| **Fastest gRPC Latency (C=1, 1 core)** | **grpc-lite (Zig)** | **30.0 µs** P50 / **39.1 µs** P99 | Leads all gRPC stacks by 17%–27% on median RTT. |
-| **Peak 8-Core Plaintext Throughput (Native)** | **Apache Thrift** | **992.6k RPC/s** (7.7× scaling) | Followed by `Cap'n Proto` (772k) and `brpc` (632k). `grpc-lite` leads gRPC (422k) before hitting a C++ client CPU ceiling. |
-| **1-Core gRPC Unary (Plaintext / TLS)** | **grpc-lite (Zig)** | **434k / 347k RPC/s** (Go client) | **4.7×** Tonic in plaintext and **4.1×** Tonic over TLS with OpenSSL 4.0.3 (up **7.18×** from the Nov 16 mbedTLS baseline). |
-| **Large Symmetric 1 MiB Payload (1 core)** | **Apache Thrift / Cap'n Proto / Tonic** | **4,394 / 4,386 / 4,382 MiB/s** | `Tonic` matches native protocols at 1 MiB; `grpc-lite` drops to last place (2,579 MiB/s / 1,289 RPC/s). |
-| **gRPC Streaming (Plaintext & TLS, 1 core)** | **grpc-lite (Zig)** / **Tonic (Rust)** | **66k** client-stream, **49k** server-stream | `grpc-lite` leads server-streaming by 1.5×–5×; `Tonic` leads Tonic-client TLS client-streaming (48.4k vs 42.7k). |
-| **gRPC C++ Callback vs. Sync API** | **Workload-dependent** | **+27%–48%** unary throughput, **3.5×** worse C=128 P99 | Callback wins on throughput across unary/multicore, but its single-core high-concurrency P99 spikes to **13.5 ms** (vs. 3.89 ms sync). |
-
-> **Scope reminder:** These matrices use different client implementations and connection topologies. **Compare frameworks within each matrix**, not by mixing numbers across matrices. Closed-loop localhost runs measure end-to-end client+server stacks, not universal isolated server ceilings.

-## Testbed & Methodology
-
-### Hardware & Isolation
-
-- **CPU:** AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX — 16 physical cores / 32 threads, `performance` scaling governor verified on CPUs `0–15`.
-- **Core pinning:** Clients pinned to physical cores `0–7` (two processes on `0–3` and `4–7` in the extended matrix); servers pinned to distinct physical cores `15` (1 core), `12–15` (4 cores), or `8–15` (8 cores).
-- **Measurement protocol:** Every formal configuration runs **3 repetitions × 5 seconds** after warmup (1 s native, 2 s extended). All reported values are **round medians**; shaded bands and whiskers in every Benchkit chart show the **full observed min–max range** across the 3 rounds. Zero RPC or response-length validation errors occurred across all 563.7M calls.
-- **No compression, retries, reflection, or request logging.** Payloads are zero-filled and response lengths are validated on every call.
-
-### Tested Software Versions
-
-| Stack | Protocol / API | Version / Commit | Runtime / Build Notes |
-| --- | --- | --- | --- |
-| **Apache Thrift** | Binary / Framed | `0.25.0` (`27e8a42`) | C++17 Release, nonblocking I/O threads |
-| **Cap'n Proto** | Two-party RPC | `1.5.0` (`373e61e`) | C++17 Release, 1 event loop/thread + `SO_REUSEPORT` |
-| **brpc** | `baidu_std` | `1.18.0` (`94f1bbd`) | C++17 Release, system protobuf 3.19.6 + OpenSSL 4 patch |
-| **grpc-lite** | gRPC / HTTP/2 | `af19148` (Zig 0.17.0) | `ReleaseFast`, `-Dtls=true` (OpenSSL 4.0.3 default; mbedTLS 3.6.6 tested in Part 3) |
-| **Tonic** | gRPC / HTTP/2 | `0.14.6` (Rust 1.100.0) | Tokio `1.53.1`, `tls-ring`, Release (`--locked`) |
-| **gRPC C++ (callback / sync)** | gRPC / HTTP/2 | `1.84.3` (GCC 16.2.1) | CMake Release, bundled protobuf `35.1.0` & Abseil `20250512` |
-| **gRPC-Go** | gRPC / HTTP/2 | `1.82.1` (Go 1.26.2) | Frozen campaign binary; matching `GOMAXPROCS` |

-## Part 1 — Cross-Protocol Plaintext Comparison (8 Frameworks)
-
-All 8 server configurations are driven by a unified closed-loop C++ load-driver harness (`harness/campaign_native.py`, managed by Benchkit). Each concurrent worker runs on its own native thread with a dedicated persistent connection (no accidental cross-worker multiplexing). All 5 gRPC servers share the exact same C++ gRPC client binary; Thrift, Cap'n Proto, and brpc use their native C++ clients under the same driver contract.
-
-### 1.1 Single-Request Latency (`C = 1`, 1 Server Core)
-
-![Single-Request Latency Across 8 RPC Frameworks](figures/01-native-latency.png)
-

-| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
-| **Apache Thrift** | 14.6 | 14.8 | **15.5** | 18.6 | **20.1** | 63,632 |
-| **Cap'n Proto** | 16.8 | 16.8 | **17.3** | 20.6 | **22.9** | 56,333 |
-| **brpc (`baidu_std`)** | 20.3 | 20.5 | **20.8** | 24.3 | **27.7** | 47,102 |
-| **grpc-lite (Zig)** | 29.0 | 29.0 | **30.0** | 33.8 | **39.1** | 32,679 |
-| **Tonic (Rust)** | 32.2 | 32.3 | **36.2** | 40.3 | **47.0** | 27,245 |
-| **gRPC-Go** | 37.1 | 37.3 | **37.8** | 42.7 | **61.2** | 25,798 |

-**Observations:**
-- Wire protocol framing dominates small-message RTT: moving from 0 B to 1 KiB adds only `0.5–4.0 µs`, whereas the baseline gap between Thrift (`15.5 µs`) and HTTP/2+gRPC (`30.0–41.0 µs`) is ~2×.
-- Among the five gRPC stacks (all measured with the identical C++ gRPC client), **`grpc-lite` is the fastest** at `30.0 µs` P50 / `39.1 µs` P99.

+| Area | Pre-Fix Bug | Fix Applied |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| **Tonic server streaming** | `streaming_output_call` spawned a Tokio task per RPC and pushed 16 responses through `mpsc::channel(1)`, throttling Tonic server-streaming to ~8.9k RPC/s. | Return `tokio_stream::iter(...)` directly without spawning or channel handoffs; increase `full_duplex_call` channel capacity to 32 ([`workloads/rust-tonic/src/main.rs`](../workloads/rust-tonic/src/main.rs)). |
+| **gRPC C++ server threading & streaming** | `cpp-server` ignored `SERVER_THREADS` (spawning host-CPU-count threads onto 1 pinned core, causing 13.5 ms P99 spikes) and flushed every streaming message individually. | Honor `SERVER_THREADS` via `SetSyncServerOption` and callback `ResourceQuota::SetMaxThreads`, enable `WriteOptions::set_buffer_hint()` on intermediate streaming messages, and add clean `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` shutdown ([`workloads/cpp-grpc/server.cc`](../workloads/cpp-grpc/server.cc)). |
+| **Cap'n Proto multicore startup race** | Each `SO_REUSEPORT` thread called `listen()` independently after spawn; the readiness probe released clients as soon as thread 0 listened, skewing connections and causing 26%–34% run-to-run spread. | Create, bind, and `listen()` on all `SO_REUSEPORT` sockets (with `SO_REUSEADDR` and `TCP_NODELAY`) before spawning worker threads ([`workloads/native-cpp/capnp.cc`](../workloads/native-cpp/capnp.cc)). |
+| **Throughput & warmup boundary accounting** | `load.h` lacked a post-warmup barrier and divided total RPCs by `max(worker.end) - begin` (straggler tail deflated high-P99 stacks); Go/Tonic clients counted drained calls against fixed `duration`; `load.h` called `Clock::now()` 3×/RPC. | Unified across Go, Rust Tonic, and C++ `load.h`: synchronized post-warmup barrier, single monotonic clock read per RPC, and unbiased per-worker active-time throughput `sum(completed_i / active_seconds_i)` ([`load.h`](../workloads/native-cpp/load.h), [`go/client/main.go`](../workloads/go/client/main.go), [`bench_client.rs`](../workloads/rust-tonic/src/bin/bench_client.rs)). |
+| **Latency recording & CPU metric skew** | Clients stored millions of raw timestamps and ran full sorts after measurement, adding GC pressure and extending `wall_seconds` while the server sat idle (diluting `server_cpu_percent`). | Replaced unbounded sample arrays with an O(1) zero-allocation log-linear histogram (8-bit mantissa, <0.4% error, <1 ms merge) across Go, Rust, and C++. |
+| **Tonic client streaming allocations** | `server-stream` allocated and dropped an unused `mpsc::channel(1)` on every RPC and allocated `Vec` templates per call. | Split `server-stream` from `bidi` and pre-allocate request templates once per worker. |
+| **Response payload buffer reuse** | Go and Tonic servers allocated and zeroed a fresh `Vec`/`[]byte` on every RPC (triggering severe Go GC at 1 MiB); C++ native clients reallocated response objects each call. | Use shared read-only zero buffers (`zeroPayload[:size]` / `Bytes::from_static`) in Go/Tonic servers and hoist/reuse response objects in C++ clients (`grpc.cc`, `brpc.cc`, `thrift.cc`). |
+| **Harness & clock bugs** | Go client stripped monotonic clock via `time.Unix(0, ...)` and dialed lazily; `run.sh` hardcoded stale `grpc-go/1.82.1`; `campaign_native.py` picked ephemeral ports; `campaign_extended.py` omitted `physical_package_id`. | Fixed Go monotonic barrier + eager `Connect()`, dynamic `go.mod`/`Cargo.toml` version detection in `run.sh`, non-ephemeral port pool `26051–26999`, and multi-socket topology check. |

-## Variability, Limits & Reproducibility
-
-### Known Variability & Methodological Limits
-- **Run-to-run spread:** Most groups exhibit `<3%` `(max - min) / median` spread across 3 rounds. The largest spreads appear in Cap'n Proto (`SO_REUSEPORT` kernel connection skew: 26% at 64 KiB, 34% at 1 MiB, 29% asymmetric) and brpc at 1 MiB (11.6%). All charts display exact observed min–max whiskers/bands so variance is transparent.
-- **Closed-loop measurement:** Does not correct for coordinated omission. Throughput includes in-flight calls drained after the 5 s deadline.
-- **Localhost TCP only:** Excludes physical NIC latency, packet loss, MTU fragmentation across switches, and NUMA/cross-host effects.
-- **Client ceilings:** `grpc-lite` on 4–8 cores hits client-side CPU limits in both the native C++ matrix and the extended Go/Tonic matrix.
-- **Non-gRPC scope:** TLS and streaming were measured for the 5 gRPC stacks only, not for Thrift, Cap'n Proto, or brpc.
-- **Aggregate latency:** Multi-process extended runs intentionally keep aggregate latency percentiles `null` rather than invalidly merging independent client histograms.

-# Full RPC comparison: grpc-lite af19148
-
-All 302 smoke and 906 formal runs passed. The formal runs completed 563,735,713
-RPCs with zero RPC or validation errors.
-
-## Results
-
-OpenSSL had higher median throughput than historical mbedTLS in all 14 TLS
-client/workload pairs. Each cell below is a throughput ratio (Go / Tonic),
-based on three-round medians:
-
-| TLS workload | New OpenSSL / old mbedTLS | New OpenSSL / new mbedTLS |
-| --- | ---: | ---: |
-| Unary, 1 KiB, 1 core | 7.18× / 6.26× | 2.21× / 1.98× |
-| Unary, 1 KiB, 4 cores | 2.72× / 2.78× | 1.00× / 1.04× |
-| Unary, 1 KiB, 8 cores | 1.64× / 1.41× | 1.02× / 0.98× |
-| Unary, 64 KiB, 1 core | 4.64× / 5.72× | 3.88× / 4.75× |
-| Client-stream, 1 core | 2.76× / 2.45× | 2.25× / 2.27× |
-| Server-stream, 1 core | 4.91× / 4.71× | 2.12× / 2.21× |
-| Bidi ping-pong, 1 core | 1.18× / 1.34× | 1.19× / 1.34× |
-
-For single-core 1 KiB unary, old mbedTLS achieved 48,320 / 43,007 RPC/s,
-new mbedTLS 156,919 / 136,016, and new OpenSSL 346,908 / 269,438.
-The historical comparison therefore includes substantial gains beyond changing
-the TLS backend. At the tested four- and eight-core loads neither current
-backend consistently wins.
-
-In the separate extended matrix, OpenSSL grpc-lite led the five gRPC server
-configurations on single-core 1 KiB TLS unary (346,546 / 265,583 RPC/s);
-Tonic was next (84,607 / 80,773). See `extended-measured/summary.tsv`.
-
-In the native plaintext eight-core, 1 KiB, concurrency-128 case, Thrift led
-at 992,615 RPC/s, followed by Cap'n Proto (772,100), brpc (632,113) and
-grpc-lite (421,511). grpc-lite led the gRPC configurations in that case but
-was last in the single-core symmetric 1 MiB case (1,289 RPC/s). These
-closed-loop localhost results are workload-specific, not capacity ceilings.
-
-## Method
-
-This campaign runs three matrices sequentially on the same host. Each formal case has three repetitions.
-
-| Matrix | Smoke runs | Formal runs | Scope |
-| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
-| TLS backend comparison | 42 | 126 | Historical `a20631f` mbedTLS, current `af19148` OpenSSL 4.0.3, current `af19148` mbedTLS 3.6.6 |
-| Native cross-protocol | 120 | 360 | grpc-lite, gRPC-Go, Tonic, C++ sync/callback, brpc, Thrift, Cap'n Proto |
-| Extended gRPC | 140 | 420 | Five gRPC server configurations, Go and Tonic clients, plaintext/TLS, unary and three streaming modes |
-
-The TLS comparison uses the previous interop reactor patch for both current builds,
-Zig 0.17.0 and `ReleaseFast`. OpenSSL is the default for `-Dtls=true`;
-`-Dtls-backend=mbedtls` selects the pinned mbedTLS package. The historical
-server and the unchanged native matrix binaries are checked against the November
-16 hash manifest; the OpenSSL binary and extended clients are checked against
-the November 21 spot check. All clients verify the same TLS certificate and
-hostname. The matrices reuse the `dd1f8f6` harness and frozen client binaries;
-the Go client runs gRPC-Go 1.82.1.
-
-In `tls/measured/comparison.tsv`, `upgrade_ratio` compares current OpenSSL to
-historical mbedTLS; `same_commit_openssl_over_mbedtls` compares current builds.
-Both divide median completed RPC/s for the same client and workload. The order
-of the three servers rotates across cases. Each streaming RPC includes 16
-messages or exchanges. `native-measured/` uses a different C++ client and
-connection layout; do not combine throughput across matrices.
-
-`run-all.sh` records the exact invocations. Stage logs sit alongside the
-measurement directories. Reproduction requires fresh stage directories. Earlier
-interrupted measurements are not inputs.

+// Log-linear histogram with 8-bit mantissa (256 sub-buckets per octave, <0.4% error,
+// exact below 512 ns, covers up to ~68.7 s) for O(1) zero-allocation latency recording.
+const HIST_SUB_BITS: u32 = 8;
+const HIST_SUB_SIZE: usize = 1 << HIST_SUB_BITS;
+const HIST_BUCKETS: usize = HIST_SUB_SIZE * 30;
+
+struct LatencyHistogram {
+    buckets: Vec<u64>,
+    count: u64,
+    sum_ns: u128,
+    min_ns: u64,
+    max_ns: u64,
+}
+
+impl LatencyHistogram {
+    fn new() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            buckets: vec![0u64; HIST_BUCKETS],
+            count: 0,
+            sum_ns: 0,
+            min_ns: 0,
+            max_ns: 0,
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn bucket(ns: u64) -> usize {
+        if ns < (2 * HIST_SUB_SIZE) as u64 {
+            return ns as usize;
+        }
+        let msb = 63 - ns.leading_zeros();
+        let shift = msb - HIST_SUB_BITS;
+        let octave = (shift + 1) as usize;
+        let sub = ((ns >> shift) as usize) & (HIST_SUB_SIZE - 1);
+        (octave * HIST_SUB_SIZE + sub).min(HIST_BUCKETS - 1)
+    }
+
+    fn value(idx: usize) -> u64 {
+        if idx < 2 * HIST_SUB_SIZE {
+            return idx as u64;
+        }
+        let octave = idx >> HIST_SUB_BITS;
+        let sub = (idx & (HIST_SUB_SIZE - 1)) as u64;
+        let shift = (octave - 1) as u32;
+        ((HIST_SUB_SIZE as u64) + sub) << shift
+    }
+
+    fn record(&mut self, ns: u64) {
+        self.buckets[Self::bucket(ns)] += 1;
+        if self.count == 0 || ns < self.min_ns {
+            self.min_ns = ns;
+        }
+        if ns > self.max_ns {
+            self.max_ns = ns;
+        }
+        self.count += 1;
+        self.sum_ns += u128::from(ns);
+    }
+
+    fn merge(&mut self, other: &Self) {
+        if other.count == 0 {
+            return;
+        }
+        if self.count == 0 || other.min_ns < self.min_ns {
+            self.min_ns = other.min_ns;
+        }
+        if other.max_ns > self.max_ns {
+            self.max_ns = other.max_ns;
+        }
+        self.count += other.count;
+        self.sum_ns += other.sum_ns;
+        for (dst, &src) in self.buckets.iter_mut().zip(other.buckets.iter()) {
+            *dst += src;
+        }
+    }

+    fn percentile_us(&self, fraction: f64) -> f64 {
+        if self.count == 0 {
+            return 0.0;
+        }
+        let rank = ((fraction * self.count as f64).ceil() as u64).max(1);
+        let mut seen = 0u64;
+        for (idx, &c) in self.buckets.iter().enumerate() {
+            seen += c;

+            }
+        }
